====大審院==== [[大審院長]]{{Efn|name="大審院長及び検事総長は親補職に"}}、[[検事総長]]{{Efn|name="大審院長及び検事総長は親補職に"}}
==親任官待遇== ===親任官の待遇を賜る官職=== 1896年（明治29年）5月1日に「親補ノ職ニ在ル者及会計検査院長待遇ノ件」（明治29年勅令第160号）により、親補の職に在る者及び会計検査院長は親任官の待遇を賜うことになる<ref name="明治29年勅令第160号親補ノ職ニ在ル者及会計検査院長待遇ノ件" /> {{Efn|name="会計検査院長は勅任官から親任官に"}} {{Efn|このとき会計検査院長の年俸は枢密顧問官や検事総長の年俸と同じ額から、枢密院議長や大審院長の年俸と同じ額に引き上げた<ref name="枢密院議長副議長顧問官並書記官長書記官議長秘書官年俸（明治24年7月27日勅令第96号） 〔明治21年勅令第23号の全部改正〕" /> <ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治２４年 |pages=161−162|chapter=会計検査院高等官年俸ノ件（明治24年7月27日勅令第97号） |id={{NDLDC|787984/129|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref> <ref name="判事検事官等俸給令（明治27年2月15日勅令第17号）" >{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治２７年 |pages=28−32|chapter=判事検事官等俸給令（明治27年2月15日勅令第17号） |id={{NDLDC|787993/85|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref> <ref name="会計検査院高等官年俸ニ関スル件（明治29年5月2日勅令第161号） 〔明治24年勅令第97号の全部改正〕" >{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治２９年 |pages=253−254|chapter=会計検査院高等官年俸ニ関スル件（明治29年5月2日勅令第161号） 〔明治24年勅令第97号の全部改正〕 |id={{NDLDC|787999/386|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref>。}}。
[[1898年]]（明治31年）7月18日に行政裁判所長官は親任官の待遇を賜うことになる<ref name="明治31年勅令第162号行政裁判所長官待遇ノ件" /> {{Efn|name="行政裁判所長官は勅任官から親任官に"}} {{Efn|このとき行政裁判所長官の年俸を枢密顧問官や検事総長の年俸と同じ額から変更しなかったが<ref name="枢密院議長副議長顧問官並書記官長書記官議長秘書官年俸（明治24年7月27日勅令第96号） 〔明治21年勅令第23号の全部改正〕" /> <ref name="判事検事官等俸給令（明治27年2月15日勅令第17号）" /> <ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治２４年 |pages=162-162 |chapter=行政裁判所長官並評定官年俸ノ件（明治24年7月27日勅令第98号） |id={{NDLDC|787984/130|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref> <ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治３１年 |page=209 |chapter=行政裁判所長官並評定官年俸ノ件中改正ノ件（明治31年7月19日勅令第163号） |id={{NDLDC|788007/285|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref>、その翌年に枢密院議長や大審院長あるいは会計検査院長の年俸と同じ額に引き上げた<ref name="枢密院議長副議長顧問官並書記官長書記官議長秘書官年俸（明治24年7月27日勅令第96号） 〔明治21年勅令第23号の全部改正〕" /> <ref name="判事検事官等俸給令（明治27年2月15日勅令第17号）" /> <ref name="会計検査院高等官年俸ニ関スル件（明治29年5月2日勅令第161号） 〔明治24年勅令第97号の全部改正〕" /> <ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治３２年 |page=179 |chapter=明治二十四年勅令第九十八号（行政裁判所長官評定官年俸ノ件）中改正ノ件（明治32年4月10日勅令第136号） |id={{NDLDC|788011/471|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref>。}}。
[[1910年]]（明治43年）8月29日に朝鮮総督府を設置した際に、旧韓国政府に属する官庁で朝鮮総督府の所属官署と見做したものに在勤中の官吏について、旧韓国法規で親任官であったものは親任官の待遇とした<ref>「御署名原本・明治四十三年・勅令第三百十九号・朝鮮総督府設置ニ関スル件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020863200、御署名原本・明治四十三年・勅令第三百十九号・朝鮮総督府設置ニ関スル件（国立公文書館）</ref>。同年9月29日に[[朝鮮総督府中枢院]]を設けて副議長を置き親任待遇とした<ref>「御署名原本・明治四十三年・勅令第三百五十五号・朝鮮総督府中枢院官制」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020866800、御署名原本・明治四十三年・勅令第三百五十五号・朝鮮総督府中枢院官制（国立公文書館）</ref>。
[[1911年]]（明治44年）7月28日に日本大[[博覧会]]会長は親任官の待遇を賜うとした<ref>「御署名原本・明治四十四年・勅令第二百十二号・日本大博覧会会長ノ待遇ニ関スル件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020909500、御署名原本・明治四十四年・勅令第二百十二号・日本大博覧会会長ノ待遇ニ関スル件（国立公文書館）</ref>
[[1916年]]（大正5年）4月14日に[[連合国 (第一次世界大戦)|連合国]]経済会議に参列させる臨時職員のうち連合国経済会議特派委員長は親任官の待遇を受けるとした<ref>「御署名原本・大正五年・勅令第百八号・連合国経済会議ニ参列セシムルタメ臨時職員設置」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021070500、御署名原本・大正五年・勅令第百八号・連合国経済会議ニ参列セシムルタメ臨時職員設置（国立公文書館）</ref>。
[[1921年]]（大正10年）3月26日に朝鮮総督府中枢院の顧問を親任待遇とした<ref> 「御署名原本・大正十年・勅令第百六十八号・朝鮮総督府中枢院官制中改正」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021323100、御署名原本・大正十年・勅令第百六十八号・朝鮮総督府中枢院官制中改正（国立公文書館）</ref>。
[[1927年]]（昭和2年）6月14日に行政制度審議会を設け、委員の待遇は官職に在るときはその官職に付き受ける待遇により、その他は親任官の待遇とした<ref>「御署名原本・昭和二年・勅令第一六八号・行政制度審議会官制」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021654000、御署名原本・昭和二年・勅令第一六八号・行政制度審議会官制（国立公文書館）</ref>。 同年12月7日に[[東京控訴院]]長である判事には親任官の待遇を賜うことになる<ref>「御署名原本・昭和二年・勅令第三四八号・東京控訴院長ノ待遇ニ関スル件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021672000、御署名原本・昭和二年・勅令第三四八号・東京控訴院長ノ待遇ニ関スル件（国立公文書館）</ref>。
[[1931年]]（昭和6年）6月20日に臨時行政財政審議会を設け、委員のうち学識経験者は親任官の待遇とした<ref>「御署名原本・昭和六年・勅令第一四〇号・臨時行政財政審議会官制（第二百五十七号ヲ以テ本号中改正第二百九十二号ヲ以テ廃止）」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021811900、御署名原本・昭和六年・勅令第一四〇号・臨時行政財政審議会官制（第二百五十七号ヲ以テ本号中改正第二百九十二号ヲ以テ廃止）（国立公文書館）</ref>。
[[1938年]]（昭和13年）9月9日に臨時に外務省に外交顧問を置き親任官の待遇とした<ref>「御署名原本・昭和十三年・勅令第六三二号・臨時外務省ニ外交顧問ヲ置クノ件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03022231000、御署名原本・昭和十三年・勅令第六三二号・臨時外務省ニ外交顧問ヲ置クノ件（国立公文書館）</ref>。
[[1944年]]（昭和19年）10月27日に臨時に内閣に[[内閣顧問]]を置き親任官の待遇とした<ref>「御署名原本・昭和十九年・勅令第六〇四号・内閣顧問臨時設置制」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03022315100、御署名原本・昭和十九年・勅令第六〇四号・内閣顧問臨時設置制（国立公文書館）</ref>。
===特に親任官の待遇を賜る者=== 特定の職にある者について、一定の年数以上在職した者や特に功績があった者は、その職自体が親任官の職とはされないものの、「親任官待遇付与奏請内規」に基づいて、親任官の待遇を与えられることがあった。同内規によれば、各帝国大学総長、北海道庁長官、警視総監、各府県知事、各省次官、内閣書記官長、法制局長官、陸軍司政長官、海軍司政長官、陸軍事務嘱託、海軍事務嘱託に一定年数在任した者が挙げられている。この他、賞勲局総裁、特命全権公使、東京工業大学長、製鉄所長官、神宮大宮司などの職にある者にも、親任官待遇が付与されることがあった。「親任官待遇付与奏請内規」（昭和17年4月28日決定）の主な内容は以下の通り。 ;親任官待遇付与奏請内規（昭和17年4月28日決定）<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 福岡県知事 吉田茂」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023540000、公文別録・親任官任免・明治二十二年～昭和二十二年・第九巻・昭和十六年～昭和十八年（国立公文書館）（第5画像目から第6画像目まで）</ref> :親任官待遇付与奏請内規左の通りこれを定む。 :勅任文官にして左の各号の一に該当し功績特に顕著なる者に対しては、特に親任官の待遇を賜うの奏請をなすことを得。 #帝国大学総長並びに京城及び台北帝国大学総長にして、一等官在職8年以上に達したる者。 #北海道庁長官、警視総監又は各府県の知事たる職に在り、一等官在職6年以上に達したる者。 #各省次官等にして、一等官在職6年以上に達したる者。 #全各号以外の勅任文官にして、一等官在職15年以上に達したる者。 #第1号又は第2号により親任官の待遇を賜う者の員数は、各3人以内とす。 :内閣書記官長又は法制局長官にしてその官歴又はその他の閲歴特に優秀なる者に付きては、特に親任官の待遇を賜うの奏請をなすことを得。 :陸軍司政長官、海軍司政長官、陸軍事務嘱託又は海軍事務嘱託にして軍占領地における枢要の職に在り識見経歴特に優秀なる者に付きては、特に親任官の待遇を賜うの奏請をなすことを得。 :かつて親任官たりし者又は親任官の待遇を賜りたる者に対しては、特に親任官の待遇を賜うの奏請をなすことを得。
;「特に親任官の待遇を賜ふ」という辞令が出た具体例 :[[片岡七郎]]（[[海軍艦政本部]]長・海軍中将）、[[1906年]]（明治39年）11月20日<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 海軍艦政本部長海軍中将 片岡七郎」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023374600、公文別録・親任官任免・明治二十二年～昭和二十二年・第二巻・明治三十二年～明治四十二年（国立公文書館）</ref>。 :[[後藤新平]]（[[拓殖局]]副総裁）、[[1910年]]（明治43年）6月20日<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 拓殖局副総裁 男爵後藤新平」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023380500、公文別録・親任官任免・明治二十二年～昭和二十二年・第三巻・明治四十三年～大正六年（国立公文書館）</ref>。 :[[一木喜徳郎]]（法制局長官）、[[1912年]]（大正元年）12月21日 <ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 法制局長官法学博士 一木喜徳郎」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023388200、公文別録・親任官任免・明治二十二年～昭和二十二年・第三巻・明治四十三年～大正六年（国立公文書館）</ref>。 :[[清野長太郎]]（[[復興局]]長官）、[[1925年]]（大正14年）9月16日<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 復興局長官 清野長太郎」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023441100、公文別録・親任官任免・明治二十二年～昭和二十二年・第五巻・大正十三年～昭和四年（国立公文書館）</ref> :[[真崎甚三郎]]（参謀次長・陸軍中将）、[[1932年]]（昭和7年）1月7日<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 参謀次長陸軍中将 真崎甚三郎」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023464200、公文別録・親任官任免・明治二十二年～昭和二十二年・第六巻・昭和五年～昭和八年（国立公文書館）（{{JACAR|A03023464200}}）</ref>。 :[[井上成美]]（海軍次官・海軍中将）、[[1944年]]（昭和19年）8月4日<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 海軍次官 井上成美」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023548800、公文別録・親任官任免・明治二十二年～昭和二十二年・第十巻・昭和十九年（国立公文書館）（{{JACAR|A03023548800}}）</ref>。
==帝国陸軍における軍事参議官制度の「悪用」== 帝国陸軍では、親補職にあった中将が、親補職でない職に就く際に、「格下げ」としないため、親補職たる軍事参議官を本職、親補職でない職を兼勤させる例があった<ref name=":9">[[額田坦]]『陸軍省人事局長の回想』（芙蓉書房、[[1977年]]〈昭和52年〉）、227頁。</ref>。最後の陸軍省人事局長であった[[額田坦]]中将は「これは軍事参議官制度の悪用というべきであろう」と評している<ref name=":9" />。
具体例。
;[[鈴木孝雄]] :[[陸軍士官学校 (日本)|陸士]][[陸軍士官学校卒業生一覧 (日本)#2期|2期]]。[[1924年]]（大正13年）2月に[[第14師団 (日本軍)|第14師団]]長に親補される。同年8月に[[陸軍技術本部]]長（非親補職）に転じる。[[1926年]]（大正15年）7月に軍事参議官に親補され、引き続き、陸軍技術本部長を兼勤。[[1927年]]（昭和2年）7月に大将に親任される。[[1928年]]（昭和3年）3月8日、陸軍技術本部長の兼勤を免じられ、軍事参議官の専任となる。[[1933年]]（昭和8年）3月に予備役。（軍事参議官が本官であった期間：1926年7月ー1933年3月、6年8か月）
;[[土肥原賢二]] :陸士[[陸軍士官学校卒業生一覧 (日本)#16期|16期]]。[[1937年]]（昭和12年）3月に[[第14師団 (日本軍)|第14師団]]長に親補される。[[1938年]]（昭和13年）6月に参謀本部付。[[1939年]]（昭和14年）5月に[[第5軍 (日本軍)|第5軍]]司令官に親補される。[[1940年]]（昭和15年）6月に参謀本部付、同年9月に軍事参議官に親補され、同年10月に[[陸軍士官学校 (日本)|陸軍士官学校長]]（非親補職）を兼勤。[[1941年]]（昭和16年）4月に大将に親任される。同年6月、軍事参議官 兼 陸軍士官学校長から、[[陸軍航空総監部|陸軍航空総監]]に親補される。（軍事参議官が本官であった期間：1940年9月ー1941年6月、0年9か月）
;[[篠塚義男]] :陸士[[陸軍士官学校卒業生一覧 (日本)#17期|17期]]。[[1938年]]（昭和13年）6月に[[第10師団 (日本軍)|第10師団]]長に親補される。[[1939年]]（昭和14年）9月に[[第1軍 (日本軍)|第1軍]]司令官に親補される。[[1941年]]（昭和16年）7月に軍事参議官に親補され、陸軍士官学校長（非親補職）を兼勤。[[1942年]]（昭和17年）7月に依願<ref>『陸軍省人事局長の回想』 411頁。</ref>予備役。（軍事参議官が本官であった期間：1941年7月ー1942年7月、1年0か月）
==前官礼遇== 親任官のうち、内閣総理大臣・国務大臣・枢密院議長・宮内大臣・内大臣の職にあった者は、一定の年数以上在職した場合、退官の後に特に勅旨を以て、前官の礼遇を付与されることがあった。前官の礼遇を受けると、[[宮中席次]]などで優遇を受けた。 ;内閣総理大臣、枢密院議長又は国務大臣たる前官礼遇付与奏請内規（昭和14年9月6日裁可） :内閣総理大臣、枢密院議長又は国務大臣たる前官礼遇付与奏請内規を左の通り定む #内閣総理大臣たる前官の礼遇は左に掲げる者にこれを賜う ##内閣総理大臣を退官したる際、左の各号の一に該当する者 ###内閣総理大臣在職4年以上の者 ###内閣総理大臣たること2回以上の者 ###かつて枢密院議長、国務大臣、宮内大臣又は内大臣たる前官の礼遇を賜りたる者 ##内閣総理大臣以外の親任官（親任官たる宮内省を含む）を退官したる際、かつて内閣総理大臣たる前官の礼遇を賜り、もしくは内閣総理大臣たりし者にして内閣総理大臣たる前官の礼遇を賜るべき資格ありたる者 #国務大臣たる前官の礼遇は左に掲げる者にこれを賜う ##国務大臣を退官したる際、左の各号の一に該当する者 ###国務大臣在職4年以上の者 ###かつて国務大臣、宮内大臣又は内大臣たる前官の礼遇を賜りたる者 ##国務大臣（内閣総理大臣を除く）以外の親任官（宮内大臣、内大臣以外の親任官たる宮内官を含む）を退官したる際、かつて国務大臣たりし者にして国務大臣、宮内大臣又は内大臣たる前官の礼遇を賜り、もしくは賜るべき資格ありたる者 #枢密院議長たる前官の礼遇は左に掲げる者にこれを賜う ##枢密院議長を退官したる際、左の各号の一に該当する者 ###枢密院議長在職4年以上の者 ###枢密院議長たること2回以上の者 ###かつて国務大臣、宮内大臣又は内大臣たる前官の礼遇を賜りたる者 ##内閣総理大臣、枢密院議長以外の親任官（親任官たる宮内官を含む）を退官したる際、かつて枢密院議長たる前官の礼遇を賜り、もしくは枢密院議長たりし者にして枢密院議長たる前官の礼遇を賜るべき資格ありたる者 #全各号の在職年数には内閣総理大臣、枢密院議長及び他の国務大臣並びに宮内大臣及び内大臣の在職年数を、回数には内閣総理大臣及び枢密院議長たりし回数を各通算す。ただし、内閣総理大臣以外の官の在職年数を内閣総理大臣の在職年数に通算する場合においては3年以上の在職年数はこれを3年とみなし、枢密院議長以外の官の在職年数を枢密院議長の在職年数に通算する場合においては3年以上の在職年数はこれを3年とみなし各通算す。 #内閣総理大臣1年以上在職したる者他の国務大臣となり退官の際国務大臣たる前官の礼遇を賜うの資格ある場合においては特に内閣総理大臣たる前官の礼遇を賜い、枢密院議長1年以上在職したる者国務大臣となり退官の際国務大臣たる前官の礼遇を賜うの資格ある場合においては特に枢密院議長たる前官の礼遇を賜う。 #宮中席次の異なる官の前官の礼遇2以上の資格ある場合においては宮中席次の高き官の前官の礼遇を賜う。 #内閣総理大臣、枢密院議長又は国務大臣と宮内大臣又は内大臣とを歴任し宮内大臣又は内大臣を退官したる際第4号本文の規定により各官の在職年数を通算して4年以上にわたる者に付きては時宜により内閣総理大臣、枢密院議長又は国務大臣たる前官の礼遇を賜う。 <!-- ;「特に前官の礼遇を賜ふ」という辞令が出た具体例。 :[[嶋田繁太郎]]海軍大将が、[[1944年]]（昭和19年）7月17日に海軍大臣を免じられた時<ref>[http://www.jacar.go.jp/DAS/meta/image_A03023544100?IS_KIND=RefSummary&IS_KEY_S1=A03023544100&IS_STYLE=default&IS_TAG_S1=reference_code& アジア歴史資料センター レファレンスコード A03023544100 『特ニ前官ノ礼遇ヲ賜フ 嶋田繁太郎』]</ref>。--><!-- 特筆性？ --> == 脚注 ==

[[File:Kanri01.png|thumb|right|300px|{{ill|Positioning of Shinninkan|ja|親任官の位置づけ|12=draft|12=draft}}]] '''Shinninkan''' (親任官) was one of the classifications of {{ill|official|ja|官吏|12=draft|12=draft}} established in 1886 (Meiji 19), and was used under the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法|lt=Meiji Constitution|lt_ja=明治憲法|12=draft|12=draft}} from 1890 (Meiji 23) until its abolition in 1947 (Showa 22)<ref>「御署名原本・明治十九年・勅令第六号・高等官官等俸給令」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020001000、御署名原本・明治十九年・勅令第六号・高等官官等俸給令（国立公文書館）</ref>. It occupied the highest rank within the {{ill|bureaucratic system|ja|官僚制度|12=draft|12=draft}} and was included among the {{ill|imperially appointed officials|ja|勅任官|12=draft|12=draft}} within the {{ill|high-ranking officials|ja|高等官|12=draft|12=draft}}. Appointment was made following the {{ill|ceremony of personal appointment|ja|親任式|12=draft|12=draft}}, and the official record ({{ill|official record|ja|官記|12=draft|12=draft}}) was personally signed by the {{ill|Emperor|ja|天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. For imperially appointed officials – including those appointed through personal appointment – the honorific {{ill|Excellency|ja|閣下|12=draft|12=draft}} was used.
Furthermore, even under the {{ill|Constitution of Japan|ja|日本国憲法|12=draft|12=draft}}, both the {{ill|Prime Minister|ja|Prime Minister of Japan|1=Prime Minister of Japan|12=draft|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Chief Justice of the Supreme Court|ja|最高裁判所長官|12=draft|12=draft}} are appointed by the Emperor through the ceremony of personal appointment; however, with the enforcement of the Constitution, the system of Shinninkan was abolished, and no official today holds the status of “Shinninkan”.<ref name="親任官廃止">「官吏任用叙級令の一部を改正する等の政令・御署名原本・昭和二十二年・政令第一〇号」国立公文書館、請求番号：御30662100（第2画像目から第5画像目まで）</ref>
==Shinninkan==
===Historical Development===
==== March 1886 (Meiji 19): High-Ranking Official Pay Regulation ==== In December 1885 (Meiji 18) on the 22nd, after defining {{ill|cabinet authority|ja|内閣職権|12=draft|12=draft}} and transitioning from the Daijō-kan system to a cabinet system, on March 12, 1886 (Meiji 19) the High-Ranking Official Pay Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 6 of Meiji 19) was issued. This regulation divided the {{ill|high-ranking officials|ja|高等官|12=draft|12=draft}} into {{ill|imperially appointed officials|ja|勅任官|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|ceremonial officials|ja|奏任官|12=draft|12=draft}}, and among the imperially appointed officials established a category for those conferred rank by means of the ceremony of personal appointment<ref name="明治19th year 3月12日勅令第6号・官等及び叙任">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15111088500|JACAR：A15111088500}}（第3画像目）</ref>. The commission document for officials appointed through personal appointment was, after the personal signature, sealed with the imperial seal and countersigned by either the {{ill|Prime Minister|ja|Prime Minister of Japan|1=Prime Minister of Japan|12=draft|12=draft}} or the senior minister<ref name="明治19th year 3月12日勅令第6号・官等及び叙任" />. Those appointed through personal appointment included the {{ill|Inner Minister|ja|内大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, the Prime Minister, the {{ill|Imperial Household Minister|ja|宮内大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, ministers of each ministry, the {{ill|Senate|ja|元老院|12=draft|12=draft}} President, generals of the Army, admirals of the Navy, the {{ill|General Staff Headquarters|ja|参謀本部|12=draft|12=draft}} Chief, and the Governor-General of the {{ill|Imperial Guard|ja|近衛|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref name="勅任官中親任ノ官ヲ定ム">「高等官ヲ分テ勅任官奏任官トシ勅任官中親任ノ官ヲ定ム」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15111105400|JACAR：A15111105400}}、公文類聚・第十編・明治十九年・第六巻・官職五・選叙任罷（国立公文書館）</ref>. Regarding the annual salaries of the civil officials among the Shinninkan, the Prime Minister’s annual salary was the same as the 12‑month salary of the former {{ill|Grand Minister|ja|太政大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, and the annual salary for each minister was equal to that of the former {{ill|first‑class official|ja|参議|12=draft|12=draft}} or first‑class officer (12‑month salary) <ref name="官禄ヲ月給ニ改定定則ヲ立並定則中改正・二条">「官禄ヲ月給ニ改定定則ヲ立並定則中改正・二条」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A24011679100、太政類典・第二編・明治四年～明治十年・第三百七巻・理財二十七・官給一（国立公文書館）（第1画像目から第5画像目まで）</ref> <ref name="明治19th year 3月12日勅令第6号・別表">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15111088500|JACAR：A15111088500}}（第7画像目）</ref>; the Inner Minister’s salary was the same as that of the other ministers<ref>「内大臣及宮中顧問官ノ年俸ヲ定ム」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A15111089900、公文類聚・第十編・明治十九年・第四巻・官職三・官等俸給（国立公文書館）</ref>, and the Senate President’s salary was set between that of the former first‑class and second‑class officials (12‑month salary each), equivalent to the highest pay for first‑class imperially appointed officials under the High‑Ranking Official Pay Regulation<ref name="官禄ヲ月給ニ改定定則ヲ立並定則中改正・二条" /> <ref name="明治19th year 3月12日勅令第6号・別表" /> <ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治８年 |pages=92−93|chapter=太政官第67号ノ2布告 元老院中正副議長議官正権大少書記官正権大中少書記生ヲ置キ官等ヲ定ム（4月25日 輪廓附）|id={{NDLDC|787955/108|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref> <ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治１９年 上巻 |pages=86−87|chapter=元老院官制（明治19th year 3月30日勅令第11号） |id={{NDLDC|787968/262|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref>.
==== July 1891 (Meiji 24): High‑Ranking Official Appointment and Pay Regulation ==== In February 1889 (Meiji 22), following the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法|12=draft|12=draft}}, and on December 24 of that year, the {{ill|cabinet system|ja|内閣官制|12=draft|12=draft}} (Imperial Ordinance No. 135 of Meiji 22) was established so that the appointment, employment, and dismissal of imperially appointed officials were to be decided by the {{ill|cabinet|ja|閣議|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>「内閣官制ヲ定ム」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A15111667400、公文類聚・第十三編・明治二十二年・第二巻・官職一・職制章程（国立公文書館）（第8画像目）</ref>.
On November 29, 1890 (Meiji 23), under the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法|12=draft|12=draft}} which came into force, on July 24, 1891 (Meiji 24) the High‑Ranking Official Appointment and Pay Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 82 of Meiji 24) was issued, thereby abolishing the previous High‑Ranking Official Pay Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 6 of Meiji 19)<ref name="明治24th year 7月24日勅令第82号">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112241100|JACAR：A15112241100}}</ref>. Although the ranks for civil and military officials were abolished, a provision continued for those among the imperially appointed officials whose appointments were made by the ceremony of personal appointment, with no change in the procedure for their commission documents<ref>{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112241100|JACAR：A15112241100}}（第1画像目）</ref> <ref>{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112241300|JACAR：A15112241300}}（第3画像目）</ref>. Regarding the annual salaries of the civil officials among the Shinninkan, the salaries for the Prime Minister and the various ministers remained the same as before<ref name="明治19th year 3月12日勅令第6号・別表" /> <ref name="明治24th year 7月24日勅令第82号・第5条">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112241100|JACAR：A15112241100}}（第2画像目）</ref>. At that time the salaries for the Privy Council positions were reduced – the President’s salary was set equal to that of the former Vice-President or the senior pay for first‑class imperially appointed officials, the Vice-President’s salary was set equal to that of the former Counselor or the lower pay for first‑class imperially appointed officials, and the Counselor’s salary was set equal to that of the former second‑class imperially appointed officials<ref name="明治19th year 3月12日勅令第6号・別表" /> <ref name="枢密院議長副議長顧問官並書記官長書記官議長秘書官年俸（明治24th year 7月27日勅令第96号） 〔明治21st year 勅令第23号の全部改正〕">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112241100|JACAR：A15112241100}}</ref>.
==== November 1891 (Meiji 24): Civil and Military High‑Ranking Official Rank Table ==== On November 14, 1891, the Civil and Military High‑Ranking Official Rank Table (Imperial Ordinance No. 215 of Meiji 24) was established, dividing the ranks of high‑ranking officials into ten classes. In this system, the imperially appointed officials were classified from first to third class; among these, the first class were those appointed through the ceremony of personal appointment – namely, the Prime Minister and various ministers<ref name="勅任官中親任ノ官ヲ定ム" />, the President, Vice‑President, and Counselor of the Privy Council<ref>「御署名原本・明治二十一年・勅令第二十二号・枢密院官制及事務規程」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020021200、御署名原本・明治二十一年・勅令第二十二号・枢密院官制及事務規程（国立公文書館）</ref>, generals/admirals, and, apart from Shinninkan and their adjunct positions, the position of the Supreme Court President<ref>「御署名原本・明治二十四年・勅令第二百十五号・文武高等官官職等級表」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020114700、御署名原本・明治二十四年・勅令第二百十五号・文武高等官官職等級表（国立公文書館）</ref>. This ranking was used as the standard for conferring rank in the internal regulation for rank progression – for instance, the initial conferral for the Prime Minister, various ministers, Privy Council President, and generals/admirals was deemed equivalent to {{ill|Third Rank (Regular)|ja|正三位|12=draft|12=draft}}, while that for the Privy Council Vice‑President and Counselor was deemed equivalent to {{ill|Third Rank (Junior)|ja|従三位|12=draft|12=draft}}, with ranks above this regarded as the utmost grade<ref>「叙位進階内則ヲ定メラル」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A15112272000、公文類聚・第十五編・明治二十四年・第十三巻・族爵・爵位・勲等・雑載（国立公文書館）（第3画像目から第6画像目まで）</ref>. Similarly, in the internal regulation for awarding decorations, this ranking was used as the standard; for example, the initial decoration for ministers, the Privy Council President, generals/admirals, and other first‑class Shinninkan was set at the second‑class decoration, with advancement possible up to the first‑class<ref>「叙勲条例並ニ附則ヲ廃シ文武官叙勲内則ヲ定ム」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A15111493500、…</ref>. However, because the High‑Ranking Official Appointment and Pay Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 82 of Meiji 24) abolished the officer ranks, when establishing the rank it had to be based solely on pay – thus, its original spirit was lost<ref name="明治25th year 勅令第96号の閣議提案">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112439800|JACAR：A15112439800}}（第1画像目から第3画像目まで）</ref>.
==== November 1892 (Meiji 25): Reestablishment of High‑Ranking Official Pay Regulation ==== On November 12, 1892 (Meiji 25), the High‑Ranking Official Pay Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 96 of Meiji 25) was issued to reestablish officer ranks, thereby abolishing both the previous High‑Ranking Official Appointment and Pay Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 82 of Meiji 24) and the Civil and Military High‑Ranking Official Rank Table (Imperial Ordinance No. 215 of Meiji 24)<ref>{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112439800|JACAR：A15112439800}}</ref>. Except for those officials appointed through the ceremony of personal appointment, the other high‑ranking officials were divided into nine classes, with those appointed by personal appointment and the first‑ and second‑class officials designated as imperially appointed officials; the procedure for the commission documents remained unchanged<ref>{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112439800|JACAR：A15112439800}}（第5画像目から第6画像目まで）</ref>. Since the criteria for officer rank and pay were not identical, the regulation was intended to allow each to develop according to its own standards – with pay continuing the Meiji 24 system, while officer rank reverted to the pre‑Meiji 24 reform system<ref name="明治25th year 勅令第96号の閣議提案" />. Accordingly, the internal regulation for rank progression was amended to use officer rank as the standard for conferral, shifting the initial decoration for the Chief of Staff from {{ill|Third Rank (Regular)|ja|正三位|12=draft|12=draft}} to {{ill|Third Rank (Junior)|ja|従三位|12=draft|12=draft}} (similar to the case for military inspectors), and likewise shifting the initial decoration for the Supreme Court President from {{ill|Fourth Rank (Regular)|ja|正四位|12=draft|12=draft}} to {{ill|Third Rank (Junior)|ja|従三位|12=draft|12=draft}} (as it was considered an adjunct position, close to military inspectors and judged to be of higher standing than the head of the Board of Audit)<ref>{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112272000|JACAR：A15112272000}}（第3画像目から第7画像目まで）</ref>. The internal regulation for awarding decorations was also amended to use officer rank as the standard – with the initial decoration for ministers, the Privy Council President, generals/admirals, and other Shinninkan set at the second‑class decoration, with advancement possible to the first‑class<ref>「叙勲内則ヲ改定セラル附叙勲内則取扱手続ヲ更定ス」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A15112452200、…</ref>.
In 1900 (Meiji 33), the internal regulation for rank progression was amended so that high‑ranking officials, after a new appointment or promotion, would receive their initial rank inscription after one month, whereas Shinninkan would receive their initial rank inscription immediately without a one‑month waiting period<ref>「文武官叙位進階内則ヲ改定セラル」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A15113342600、…</ref>{{efn|This amendment was necessary to prevent the criticism of excessively generous conferrals of high rank, and thus the initial ranks for Shinninkan and those below were corrected<ref>{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15113342600|JACAR：A15113342600}}（第4画像目）</ref>.}}
==== April 1946 (Showa 21): The Official Appointment and Rank Regulation ==== Following Japan’s acceptance of the {{ill|Potsdam Declaration|ja|ポツダム宣言|12=draft|12=draft}} in 1945 (Showa 20), on April 1, 1946 (Showa 21) the Official Appointment and Rank Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 190 of Showa 21) was promulgated and enforced under the Allied occupation<ref name="昭和21st year 勅令第190号官吏任用叙級令">「御署名原本・昭和二十一年・勅令第一九〇号・官吏任用叙級令」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A04017814300、御署名原本・昭和二十一年・勅令第一九〇号・官吏任用叙級令（国立公文書館）（第2画像目）</ref>. In this regulation, other officials (excluding those appointed by personal appointment) were divided into first-, second-, and third‑class officials, and at the same time the High‑Ranking Official Pay Regulation was abolished – with the terms changed so that “imperially appointed officials” became “first‑class officials”, “ceremonial officials” became “second‑class officials”, and “high‑ranking officials” became “first‑ or second‑class officials”<ref name="昭和21st year 4月1日勅令第193号・高等官官等俸給令廃止">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A04017814600|JACAR：A04017814600}}（第2画像目から第3画像目まで）</ref>; however, officials appointed by personal appointment (Shinninkan) were retained<ref name="昭和21st year 勅令第190号官吏任用叙級令" /> <ref>「御署名原本・昭和二十一年・勅令第一九一号・親任官及諸官級別令」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A04017814400、御署名原本・昭和二十一年・勅令第一九一号・親任官及諸官級別令（国立公文書館）</ref>.
On May 2, 1947 (Showa 22), amendments were made to the Official Appointment and Rank Regulation to revise the provisions concerning officials appointed by personal appointment (excluding special officials), dividing the remaining officials into first-, second‑, and third‑class categories<ref>{{Cite journal|和書|editor=大蔵省印刷局|date=1947-05-02|year=1947|title=官吏任用叙級令の一部を改正する等に関する勅令（昭和22nd year 5月2日勅令第205号）|journal=官報|volume=1947th year 05月02日|issue=物価号外|page=1|publisher=日本マイクロ写真|location=東京|language=ja|accessdate=2024-11-05}}</ref>, and on the following day, with the enforcement of the {{ill|Constitution of Japan|ja|日本国憲法|12=draft|12=draft}}, further amendments were made to conform the regulation to Article 15 of the Constitution by abolishing the provisions for officials appointed by personal appointment (Shinninkan)<ref name="親任官廃止"/><ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.jacar.go.jp/glossary/tochikiko-henten/qa/qa31.html|title=When did the civil service and diplomatic service examinations begin?|accessdate=2024-11-06|author=国立公文書館 アジア歴史資料センター|authorlink=アジア歴史資料センター|website=アジア歴史資料センター|publisher=国立公文書館}}</ref>. Furthermore, whereas previously the Prime Minister, various ministers, and other Shinninkan were appointed by personal appointment, under the new procedures the Prime Minister and the {{ill|Chief Justice of the Supreme Court|ja|最高裁判所長官|12=draft|12=draft}} are appointed by the Emperor pursuant to Article 6 of the {{ill|Constitution of Japan|ja|日本国憲法|12=draft|12=draft}} and related laws<ref>{{Cite journal|和書|editor=大蔵省印刷局|date=1947-04-16|year=1947|title=裁判所法（昭和22nd year 4月16日法律第59号）|journal=官報|volume=昭和|issue=6047|page=118|publisher=日本マイクロ写真|location=東京|language=ja|accessdate=2024-11-10}}</ref>, and other officials’ appointments are certified by the Emperor as part of state acts under Article 7 of the Constitution. The procedure for the Prime Minister’s nomination involves submission by the Speaker of the House of Representatives through the cabinet<ref>{{Cite journal|和書|editor=大蔵省印刷局|date=1947-04-30|year=1947|title=国会法（昭和22nd year 4月30日法律第79号）|journal=官報|volume=昭和|issue=6085|page=283|publisher=日本マイクロ写真|location=東京|language=ja|accessdate=2024-11-10}}</ref>, and the certification of appointment for officials is made by the Prime Minister<ref>{{Cite journal|和書|editor=大蔵省印刷局|date=1947-05-03|year=1947|title=官吏の任免、叙級、休職、復職その他の官吏の身分上の事項に関する手続に関する政令（昭和22nd year 5月3日政令第11号）|journal=官報|volume=1947th year 05月03日|issue=物価号外|page=5|publisher=日本マイクロ写真|location=東京|language=ja|accessdate=2024-11-04}}</ref>.
===Civil Officials=== Civil officials include the {{ill|Prime Minister|ja|Prime Minister of Japan|1=Prime Minister of Japan|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Director of the Japan–Manchuria Affairs Office|ja|対満事務局総裁|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|President of the Privy Council|ja|枢密院議長|12=draft|12=draft}}, the Vice‑President and the Counselor of the Privy Council, the {{ill|Inner Minister|ja|内大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Imperial Household Minister|ja|宮内大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Minister of State|ja|国務大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|文官としての立場での陸軍大臣および海軍大臣も含む。}}</ref>, the {{ill|Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary|ja|特命全権大使|12=draft|12=draft}}, Shinninkan {{ill|judges|ja|判事|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|大審院長及び検事総長は親補職に｜判事は陸海軍将校と同様に終身官であり、検事は裁判所構成法に基づき解任されにくい。}}</ref>, Shinninkan {{ill|prosecutors|ja|検事|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|大審院長及び検事総長は親補職に}}</ref>, the {{ill|Head of the Board of Audit|ja|会計検査院長|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|明治22nd year に会計検査院法制定当初は勅任官であったが、その後親任官へ昇格。}}</ref>, the {{ill|Chief of the Administrative Court|ja|行政裁判所長官|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|明治23rd year に行政裁判法制定当初は勅任官であったが、後に親任官へ。}}</ref>, the {{ill|Governor-General of Korea|ja|朝鮮総督|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|官制では陸海軍大将が任用されるが、後に文官任用も可能となった。}}</ref>, the {{ill|Chief Administrative Officer of the Korean Governor-General's Office|ja|朝鮮総督府政務総監|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Governor of Taiwan|ja|台湾総督|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|官制では陸海軍大将または中将が任用される予定であったが、後に文官任用も可能となり実際には文官が任用された。}}</ref>, the {{ill|Shrine Festival Master|ja|神宮祭主|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|President of the Planning Institute|ja|企画院総裁|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Governor of Tokyo|ja|東京都長官|12=draft|12=draft}}, and the {{ill|Regional Governor-General|ja|地方総監|12=draft|12=draft}} among others.
===Military Officials=== Military officials include the {{ill|General of the Army|ja|陸軍大将|12=draft|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Admiral of the Fleet|ja|海軍大将|12=draft|12=draft}}.
==Assistant Positions (Shinpōshoku)== Military officials were distinguished from civil officials by a separate system of appointment and duty orders. In particular, officers were regarded as lifetime officials – even after retirement they retained their rank. (For example, military officers were classified into active, standby, suspended, or dismissed statuses, and in the case of army officers these classifications were set by earlier regulations; see also the explanatory notes in the “Regulations on Military Officer Appointments”<ref>「陸軍将校免黜条例」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A24011241400、…</ref>.) Consequently, after December 2, 1890 (Meiji 23), the only military officials designated as Shinninkan were the General of the Army and the Admiral of the Fleet<ref>{{efn|明治19th year に初めて親任官を定めた際、陸軍大将、海軍大将に加え、参謀本部長および近衛都督も含まれていたが、その後は大将のみとなった。}}</ref>. Judicial officials were also treated separately – their titles (judge or prosecutor) were kept distinct from their duties, with the Head of the Supreme Court and the Chief Prosecutor regarded as adjunct positions<ref>{{efn|大審院長及び検事総長は親補職に}}</ref>. On November 29, 1890 (Meiji 23), under the Constitution which came into force that year, on December 2 the Regulations for the General Staff (Imperial Ordinance No. 25 of Meiji 22)<ref>「御署名原本・明治二十二年・勅令第二十五号・参謀本部条例制定参軍官制、陸軍参謀本部条例、海軍参謀本部条例廃止」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020035900、…</ref> and the Regulations for the Army Inspection Department (Imperial Ordinance No. 18 of Meiji 20)<ref>「御署名原本・明治二十年・勅令第十八号・監軍部条例」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020011600、…</ref> were amended so that one general or lieutenant general was appointed as the Chief of Staff for the entire Imperial Army and supplemented as an assistant, while one inspector was appointed in the Army Inspection Department and similarly supplemented using a general or lieutenant general<ref name="明治23rd year 勅令第279号参謀本部条例第二条中改正" /> <ref name="明治23rd year 勅令第280号監軍部条例第二条改正" />{{efn|In the Navy, on May 19, 1893 (Meiji 26), a similar amendment was made in the Naval Command Regulations (Imperial Ordinance No. 37 of Meiji 26) to have a general or lieutenant general supplement the Commander of the Naval Command.}}</ref>. In this way, by the Emperor’s {{ill|personal adjunction ceremony|ja|親補式|12=draft|12=draft}}, the position of “Assistant Position (Shinpōshoku)” was established.
On May 1, 1896 (Meiji 29), the document “Matters concerning the Treatment of Those in Assistant Positions and the Head of the Board of Audit” (Imperial Ordinance No. 160 of Meiji 29) stipulated that those holding assistant positions and the Head of the Board of Audit were to receive Shinninkan treatment<ref name="明治29th year 勅令第160号親補ノ職ニ在ル者及会計検査院長待遇ノ件">「親補ノ職ニ在ル者及会計検査院長待遇ノ件」</ref>. The assistant positions were defined within the military hierarchy and, while holding those positions, the officials received Shinninkan treatment<ref name=":0" />. Although no specific rank was prescribed, the military regulations stated that “assistant positions are to be supplemented by a general or lieutenant general,” so it was not possible for officers below major general to be treated as Shinninkan<ref>{{efn|…}}</ref>. (For instance, in peacetime the divisional commander was not considered “supplemented” by a general but by a lieutenant general, being the largest formation directly controlled by the Emperor<ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治２１年 |pages=77−80|chapter=師団司令部条例（明治21st year 5月14日勅令第27号）|id={{NDLDC|787973/100|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref>{{efn|Examples include cases where a divisional commander in office as a lieutenant general was later conferred Shinninkan status upon promotion to general (e.g. [[長谷川好道]]), or when a divisional commander died in battle and was posthumously promoted to general (e.g. [[栗林忠道]]).}}</ref>. Also, because the Army Minister and the Navy Minister held both military and civil roles, even if they were lieutenant generals, they could issue administrative orders to generals<ref>奥宮正武『大艦巨砲主義の盛衰』〈新戦史シリーズ47〉、朝日ソノラマ、1992nd year 、318頁。</ref>.

==Treatment as Shinninkan==
===Positions Receiving Shinninkan Treatment=== On May 1, 1896 (Meiji 29), the document “Matters concerning the Treatment of Those in Assistant Positions and the Head of the Board of Audit” (Imperial Ordinance No. 160 of Meiji 29) provided that those holding assistant positions and the Head of the Board of Audit were to receive the treatment of Shinninkan<ref name="明治29th year 勅令第160号親補ノ職ニ在ル者及会計検査院長待遇ノ件">「親補ノ職ニ在ル者及会計検査院長待遇ノ件」</ref>{{efn|会計検査院長 was elevated from an imperially appointed official to Shinninkan status.}}. On July 18, 1898 (Meiji 31), the Chief of the Administrative Court was accorded Shinninkan treatment<ref name="明治31st year 勅令第162号行政裁判所長官待遇ノ件">「御署名原本・明治三十一年・勅令第百六十二号・行政裁判所長官待遇ノ件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020346100、…</ref>{{efn|Although his salary was initially unchanged from that of the Privy Council Counselor or Chief Prosecutor, it was raised the following year to match that of the Privy Council President or the Head of the Board of Audit.}}. In the following year his salary was raised to that of the Privy Council President, the Chief Justice, or the Head of the Board of Audit<ref name="枢密院議長副議長顧問官並書記官長書記官議長秘書官年俸（明治24th year 7月27日勅令第96号） 〔明治21st year 勅令第23号の全部改正〕" /> <ref name="判事検事官等俸給令（明治27th year 2月15日勅令第17号）" /> <ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治３２年 |page=179|chapter=明治二十四年勅令第九十八号（行政裁判所長官評定官年俸ノ件）中改正ノ件（明治32nd year 4月10日勅令第136号）|id={{NDLDC|788011/471|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref>.
On August 29, 1910 (Meiji 43), when the {{ill|Governor-General of Korea|ja|朝鮮総督府|12=draft|12=draft}} was established, officials from the former Korean government’s agencies who were considered part of the new Governor-General’s Office and who had previously been treated as Shinninkan under Korean law were granted Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・明治四十三年・勅令第三百十九号・朝鮮総督府設置ニ関スル件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020863200、…</ref>. In September of the same year, a Central Council ({{ill|Korean Governor-General’s Central Council|ja|朝鮮総督府中枢院|12=draft|12=draft}}) was established and its Vice-President was accorded Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・明治四十三年・勅令第三百五十五号・朝鮮総督府中枢院官制」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020866800、…</ref>.
On July 28, 1911 (Meiji 44), the President of the {{ill|Japan Exhibition|ja|博覧会|12=draft|12=draft}} was granted Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・明治四十四年・勅令第二百十二号・日本大博覧会会長ノ待遇ニ関スル件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020909500、…</ref>.
On April 14, 1916 (Taisho 5), among temporary staff sent to attend the Allied Economic Conference, the Special Commissioner for the conference was accorded Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・大正五年・勅令第百八号・連合国経済会議ニ参列セシムルタメ臨時職員設置」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021070500、…</ref>.
On March 26, 1921 (Taisho 10), the advisor to the Korean Governor-General’s Central Council was granted Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・大正十年・勅令第百六十八号・朝鮮総督府中枢院官制中改正」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021323100、…</ref>.
On June 14, 1927 (Showa 2), an Administrative System Deliberation Council was established; for its members, if serving in an official capacity they received treatment according to their office, otherwise they were given Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・昭和二年・勅令第一六八号・行政制度審議会官制」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021654000、…</ref>. On December 7 of the same year, the President of the {{ill|Tokyo Appellate Court|ja|東京控訴院長|12=draft|12=draft}} was granted Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・昭和二年・勅令第三四八号・東京控訴院長ノ待遇ニ関スル件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021672000、…</ref>.
On June 20, 1931 (Showa 6), an ad hoc Administrative and Financial Deliberation Council was established, and among its members those with academic or professional expertise were granted Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・昭和六年・勅令第一四〇号・臨時行政財政審議会官制（第二百五十七号ヲ以テ本号中改正第二百九十二号ヲ以テ廃止）」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021811900、…</ref>.
On September 9, 1938 (Showa 13), an ad hoc diplomatic advisor position was created within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and was accorded Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・昭和十三年・勅令第六三二号・臨時外務省ニ外交顧問ヲ置クノ件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03022231000、…</ref>.
On October 27, 1944 (Showa 19), an ad hoc Cabinet Advisor position was established and granted Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・昭和十九年・勅令第六〇四号・内閣顧問臨時設置制」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03022315100、…</ref>.
===Particularly, Those Granted Special Shinninkan Treatment=== For certain positions, officials who had served a prescribed number of years or rendered especially distinguished service – even if their office was not inherently a Shinninkan position – could be granted Shinninkan treatment based on the “Internal Regulation for Granting Shinninkan Treatment.” According to this regulation, the following officials were eligible:
;Internal Regulation for Granting Shinninkan Treatment (Decided April 28, Showa 17) :The regulation is defined as follows: :For imperially appointed civil officials who satisfy one of the following and have rendered especially outstanding service, a petition for granting Shinninkan treatment may be submitted: # Presidents of Imperial Universities and of the Keijo and Taipei Imperial Universities who have served as first‑class officials for 8 or more years. # Heads of the Hokkaido Prefecture, police commissioners, or prefectural governors who have served as first‑class officials for 6 or more years. # Deputy ministers of each ministry who have served as first‑class officials for 6 or more years. # Other imperially appointed civil officials who have served as first‑class officials for 15 or more years. # In cases under either clause 1 or 2, the number of officials granted Shinninkan treatment is limited to three per category. :Additionally, Cabinet Secretaries or Directors of the Legal Bureau with particularly outstanding records may be petitioned for special Shinninkan treatment. :Similarly, for Army or Navy administrative officers with important roles in occupied areas and outstanding service records, a petition may be submitted. :Moreover, those who have previously held Shinninkan status or received such treatment may also be considered.
;Examples of specific decrees granting “special Shinninkan treatment”: * [[片岡七郎]] (Head of the Naval Administration Headquarters, Navy Lieutenant General), November 20, 1906 (Meiji 39)<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 海軍艦政本部長海軍中将 片岡七郎」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023374600、…</ref>. * [[後藤新平]] (Vice-President of the Settlement Bureau), June 20, 1910 (Meiji 43)<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 拓殖局副総裁 男爵後藤新平」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023380500、…</ref>. * [[一木喜徳郎]] (Director of the Legal Bureau), December 21, 1912 (Taisho 1)<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 法制局長官法学博士 一木喜徳郎」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023388200、…</ref>. * [[清野長太郎]] (Head of the Reconstruction Bureau), September 16, 1925 (Taisho 14)<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 復興局長官 清野長太郎」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023441100、…</ref>. * [[真崎甚三郎]] (Vice Chief of Staff, Army Lieutenant General), January 7, 1932 (Showa 7)<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 参謀次長陸軍中将 真崎甚三郎」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023464200、…</ref>. * [[井上成美]] (Deputy Navy Minister, Navy Lieutenant General), August 4, 1944 (Showa 19)<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 海軍次官 井上成美」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023548800、…</ref>.
==Abuse of the Military Councilor System in the Imperial Army== In the Imperial Army, there were cases in which a lieutenant general holding an assistant (Shinpōshoku) position would concurrently hold a non‑assistant post without a formal demotion – effectively using the position of Military Councilor as his principal office. Lieutenant General [[額田坦]], the last Chief of the Army Personnel Bureau, commented, “This should be regarded as an abuse of the Military Councilor system.”<ref name=":9">[[額田坦]]『陸軍省人事局長の回想』（芙蓉書房、1977〈昭和52nd year 〉）、227頁。</ref>
For example:
; [[鈴木孝雄]] : An army officer (2nd term graduate of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Academy|ja|陸軍士官学校|12=draft|12=draft}}). In February 1924 (Taisho 13) he was supplemented as the commander of the {{ill|14th Division|ja|第14師団|12=draft|12=draft}}. In August of the same year he was transferred to serve as the head of the {{ill|Army Technical Headquarters|ja|陸軍技術本部|12=draft|12=draft}} (a non‑assistant position). In July 1926 (Taisho 15) he was supplemented as a Military Councilor while continuing as head of the Army Technical Headquarters. In July 1927 (Showa 2) he was appointed as a general, and on March 8, 1928 (Showa 3) he ceased concurrently serving as head of the Army Technical Headquarters and became exclusively a Military Councilor. (He served as a Military Councilor in his principal role from July 1926 to March 1933 – a total of 6 years and 8 months.)
; [[土肥原賢二]] : An army officer (16th term graduate of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Academy|ja|陸軍士官学校|12=draft|12=draft}}). In March 1937 (Showa 12) he was supplemented as the commander of the {{ill|14th Division|ja|第14師団|12=draft|12=draft}}. In June 1938 (Showa 13) he was assigned to the General Staff. In May 1939 (Showa 14) he was supplemented as the commander of the {{ill|5th Army|ja|第5軍|12=draft|12=draft}}, and in June 1940 (Showa 15) returned to the General Staff; later in September of that year he was supplemented as a Military Councilor and in October he concurrently assumed the post of {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Academy|ja|陸軍士官学校|12=draft|12=draft}} Head (a non‑assistant position). In April 1941 (Showa 16) he was appointed as a general; in June he was supplemented as the Army Air Service Chief. (He served as Military Councilor in his principal role from September 1940 to June 1941 – a total of 9 months.)
; [[篠塚義男]] : An army officer (17th term graduate of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Academy|ja|陸軍士官学校|12=draft|12=draft}}). In June 1938 (Showa 13) he was supplemented as the commander of the {{ill|10th Division|ja|第10師団|12=draft|12=draft}}. In September 1939 (Showa 14) he was supplemented as the commander of the {{ill|1st Army|ja|第1軍|12=draft|12=draft}}. In July 1941 (Showa 16) he was supplemented as a Military Councilor while concurrently serving as the Head of the Imperial Japanese Army Academy (a non‑assistant position). In July 1942 (Showa 17) he entered the reserves on request<ref>『陸軍省人事局長の回想』 411頁。</ref> (He served as Military Councilor in his principal role from July 1941 to July 1942 – a total of 1 year).
==Former Official Honors== Among the Shinninkan, those who held offices such as the {{ill|Prime Minister|ja|Prime Minister of Japan|1=Prime Minister of Japan|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minister of State|ja|国務大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|President of the Privy Council|ja|枢密院議長|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Imperial Household Minister|ja|宮内大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Inner Minister|ja|内大臣|12=draft|12=draft}} would, if they had served for a sufficient number of years, upon retirement be granted former official honors by special imperial decree. Such honors—conferring, for example, preferential seating at the {{ill|Imperial Court Order|ja|宮中席次|12=draft|12=draft}}—were awarded as follows:
; Former Official Honor Award Regulation for the Prime Minister (Approved September 6, Showa 14) : The regulation is set out as follows: # For former Prime Ministers who served for at least 4 years. # For those who served as Prime Minister more than twice. # And for those who had previously received former official honors as either the Privy Council President, Minister of State, Imperial Household Minister, or Inner Minister. ; (Similar provisions apply for former Ministers of State and for former Privy Council Presidents, with detailed clauses on how service years are totaled.)

[[File:Kanri01.png|thumb|right|300px|{{ill|Positioning of Shinninkan|ja|親任官の位置づけ|12=draft|12=draft}}]] '''Shinninkan''' (親任官) was one of the classifications of {{ill|official|ja|官吏|12=draft|12=draft}} established in 1886 (Meiji 19), and was used under the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法|lt=Meiji Constitution|lt_ja=明治憲法|12=draft|12=draft}} from 1890 (Meiji 23) until its abolition in 1947 (Showa 22)<ref>「御署名原本・明治十九年・勅令第六号・高等官官等俸給令」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020001000、御署名原本・明治十九年・勅令第六号・高等官官等俸給令（国立公文書館）</ref>. It occupied the highest Rank within the {{ill|bureaucratic system|ja|官僚制度|12=draft|12=draft}} and was included among the {{ill|imperially appointed officials|ja|勅任官|12=draft|12=draft}} within the {{ill|high-Ranking officials|ja|高等官|12=draft|12=draft}}. Appointment was made following the {{ill|ceremony of personal appointment|ja|親任式|12=draft|12=draft}}, and the official record ({{ill|official record|ja|官記|12=draft|12=draft}}) was personally signed by the {{ill|Emperor|ja|天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. For imperially appointed officials – including those appointed through personal appointment – the honorific {{ill|Excellency|ja|閣下|12=draft|12=draft}} was used.
Furthermore, even under the {{ill|Constitution of Japan|ja|日本国憲法|12=draft|12=draft}}, both the {{ill|Prime Minister|ja|Prime Minister of Japan|1=Prime Minister of Japan|12=draft|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Chief Justice of the Supreme Court|ja|最高裁判所長官|12=draft|12=draft}} are appointed by the Emperor through the ceremony of personal appointment; however, with the enforcement of the Constitution, the system of Shinninkan was abolished, and no official today holds the status of “Shinninkan”.<ref name="親任官廃止">「官吏任用叙級令の一部を改正する等の政令・御署名原本・昭和二十二年・政令第一〇号」国立公文書館、請求番号：御30662100（第2画像目から第5画像目まで）</ref>
==Shinninkan==
===Historical Development===
==== March 1886 (Meiji 19): High-Ranking Official Pay Regulation ==== In December 1885 (Meiji 18) on the 22nd, after defining {{ill|cabinet authority|ja|内閣職権|12=draft|12=draft}} and transitioning from the Daijō-kan system to a cabinet system, on March 12, 1886 (Meiji 19) the High-Ranking Official Pay Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 6 of Meiji 19) was issued. This regulation divided the {{ill|high-Ranking officials|ja|高等官|12=draft|12=draft}} into {{ill|imperially appointed officials|ja|勅任官|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|ceremonial officials|ja|奏任官|12=draft|12=draft}}, and among the imperially appointed officials established a category for those conferred Rank by means of the ceremony of personal appointment<ref name="明治19th year 3月12日勅令第6号・官等及び叙任">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15111088500|JACAR：A15111088500}}（第3画像目）</ref>. The commission document for officials appointed through personal appointment was, after the personal signature, sealed with the imperial seal and countersigned by either the {{ill|Prime Minister|ja|Prime Minister of Japan|1=Prime Minister of Japan|12=draft|12=draft}} or the senior minister<ref name="明治19th year 3月12日勅令第6号・官等及び叙任" />. Those appointed through personal appointment included the {{ill|Inner Minister|ja|内大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, the Prime Minister, the {{ill|Imperial Household Minister|ja|宮内大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, ministers of each ministry, the {{ill|Senate|ja|元老院|12=draft|12=draft}} President, generals of the Army, admirals of the Navy, the {{ill|General Staff Headquarters|ja|参謀本部|12=draft|12=draft}} Chief, and the Governor-General of the {{ill|Imperial Guard|ja|近衛|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref name="勅任官中親任ノ官ヲ定ム">「高等官ヲ分テ勅任官奏任官トシ勅任官中親任ノ官ヲ定ム」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15111105400|JACAR：A15111105400}}、公文類聚・第十編・明治十九年・第六巻・官職五・選叙任罷（国立公文書館）</ref>. Regarding the annual salaries of the civil officials among the Shinninkan, the Prime Minister’s annual salary was the same as the 12‑month salary of the former {{ill|Grand Minister|ja|太政大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, and the annual salary for each minister was equal to that of the former {{ill|first‑class official|ja|参議|12=draft|12=draft}} or first‑class officer (12‑month salary) <ref name="官禄ヲ月給ニ改定定則ヲ立並定則中改正・二条">「官禄ヲ月給ニ改定定則ヲ立並定則中改正・二条」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A24011679100、太政類典・第二編・明治四年～明治十年・第三百七巻・理財二十七・官給一（国立公文書館）（第1画像目から第5画像目まで）</ref> <ref name="明治19th year 3月12日勅令第6号・別表">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15111088500|JACAR：A15111088500}}（第7画像目）</ref>; the Inner Minister’s salary was the same as that of the other ministers<ref>「内大臣及宮中顧問官ノ年俸ヲ定ム」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A15111089900、公文類聚・第十編・明治十九年・第四巻・官職三・官等俸給（国立公文書館）</ref>, and the Senate President’s salary was set between that of the former first‑class and second‑class officials (12‑month salary each), equivalent to the highest pay for first‑class imperially appointed officials under the High‑Ranking Official Pay Regulation<ref name="官禄ヲ月給ニ改定定則ヲ立並定則中改正・二条" /> <ref name="明治19th year 3月12日勅令第6号・別表" /> <ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治８年 |pages=92−93|chapter=太政官第67号ノ2布告 元老院中正副議長議官正権大少書記官正権大中少書記生ヲ置キ官等ヲ定ム（4月25日 輪廓附）|id={{NDLDC|787955/108|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref> <ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治１９年 上巻 |pages=86−87|chapter=元老院官制（明治19th year 3月30日勅令第11号） |id={{NDLDC|787968/262|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref>.
==== July 1891 (Meiji 24): High‑Ranking Official Appointment and Pay Regulation ==== In February 1889 (Meiji 22), following the promulgation of the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法|12=draft|12=draft}}, and on December 24 of that year, the {{ill|cabinet system|ja|内閣官制|12=draft|12=draft}} (Imperial Ordinance No. 135 of Meiji 22) was established so that the appointment, employment, and dismissal of imperially appointed officials were to be decided by the {{ill|cabinet|ja|閣議|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>「内閣官制ヲ定ム」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A15111667400、公文類聚・第十三編・明治二十二年・第二巻・官職一・職制章程（国立公文書館）（第8画像目）</ref>.
On November 29, 1890 (Meiji 23), under the {{ill|Constitution of the Empire of Japan|ja|大日本帝国憲法|12=draft|12=draft}} which came into force, on July 24, 1891 (Meiji 24) the High‑Ranking Official Appointment and Pay Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 82 of Meiji 24) was issued, thereby abolishing the previous High‑Ranking Official Pay Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 6 of Meiji 19)<ref name="明治24th year 7月24日勅令第82号">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112241100|JACAR：A15112241100}}</ref>. Although the Ranks for civil and military officials were abolished, a provision continued for those among the imperially appointed officials whose appointments were made by the ceremony of personal appointment, with no change in the procedure for their commission documents<ref>{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112241100|JACAR：A15112241100}}（第1画像目）</ref> <ref>{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112241300|JACAR：A15112241300}}（第3画像目）</ref>. Regarding the annual salaries of the civil officials among the Shinninkan, the salaries for the Prime Minister and the various ministers remained the same as before<ref name="明治19th year 3月12日勅令第6号・別表" /> <ref name="明治24th year 7月24日勅令第82号・第5条">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112241100|JACAR：A15112241100}}（第2画像目）</ref>. At that time the salaries for the Privy Council positions were reduced – the President’s salary was set equal to that of the former Vice-President or the senior pay for first‑class imperially appointed officials, the Vice-President’s salary was set equal to that of the former Counselor or the lower pay for first‑class imperially appointed officials, and the Counselor’s salary was set equal to that of the former second‑class imperially appointed officials<ref name="明治19th year 3月12日勅令第6号・別表" /> <ref name="枢密院議長副議長顧問官並書記官長書記官議長秘書官年俸（明治24th year 7月27日勅令第96号） 〔明治21st year 勅令第23号の全部改正〕">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112241100|JACAR：A15112241100}}</ref>.
==== November 1891 (Meiji 24): Civil and Military High‑Ranking Official Rank Table ==== On November 14, 1891, the Civil and Military High‑Ranking Official Rank Table (Imperial Ordinance No. 215 of Meiji 24) was established, dividing the Ranks of high‑Ranking officials into ten classes. In this system, the imperially appointed officials were classified from first to third class; among these, the first class were those appointed through the ceremony of personal appointment – namely, the Prime Minister and various ministers<ref name="勅任官中親任ノ官ヲ定ム" />, the President, Vice‑President, and Counselor of the Privy Council<ref>「御署名原本・明治二十一年・勅令第二十二号・枢密院官制及事務規程」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020021200、御署名原本・明治二十一年・勅令第二十二号・枢密院官制及事務規程（国立公文書館）</ref>, generals/admirals, and, apart from Shinninkan and their adjunct positions, the position of the Supreme Court President<ref>「御署名原本・明治二十四年・勅令第二百十五号・文武高等官官職等級表」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020114700、御署名原本・明治二十四年・勅令第二百十五号・文武高等官官職等級表（国立公文書館）</ref>. This Ranking was used as the standard for conferring Rank in the internal regulation for Rank progression – for instance, the initial conferral for the Prime Minister, various ministers, Privy Council President, and generals/admirals was deemed equivalent to {{ill|Third Rank (Regular)|ja|正三位|12=draft|12=draft}}, while that for the Privy Council Vice‑President and Counselor was deemed equivalent to {{ill|Third Rank (Junior)|ja|従三位|12=draft|12=draft}}, with Ranks above this regarded as the utmost grade<ref>「叙位進階内則ヲ定メラル」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A15112272000、公文類聚・第十五編・明治二十四年・第十三巻・族爵・爵位・勲等・雑載（国立公文書館）（第3画像目から第6画像目まで）</ref>. Similarly, in the internal regulation for awarding decorations, this Ranking was used as the standard; for example, the initial decoration for ministers, the Privy Council President, generals/admirals, and other first‑class Shinninkan was set at the second‑class decoration, with advancement possible up to the first‑class<ref>「叙勲条例並ニ附則ヲ廃シ文武官叙勲内則ヲ定ム」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A15111493500、…</ref>. However, because the High‑Ranking Official Appointment and Pay Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 82 of Meiji 24) abolished the officer Ranks, when establishing the Rank it had to be based solely on pay – thus, its original spirit was lost<ref name="明治25th year 勅令第96号の閣議提案">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112439800|JACAR：A15112439800}}（第1画像目から第3画像目まで）</ref>.
==== November 1892 (Meiji 25): Reestablishment of High‑Ranking Official Pay Regulation ==== On November 12, 1892 (Meiji 25), the High‑Ranking Official Pay Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 96 of Meiji 25) was issued to reestablish officer Ranks, thereby abolishing both the previous High‑Ranking Official Appointment and Pay Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 82 of Meiji 24) and the Civil and Military High‑Ranking Official Rank Table (Imperial Ordinance No. 215 of Meiji 24)<ref>{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112439800|JACAR：A15112439800}}</ref>. Except for those officials appointed through the ceremony of personal appointment, the other high‑Ranking officials were divided into nine classes, with those appointed by personal appointment and the first‑ and second‑class officials designated as imperially appointed officials; the procedure for the commission documents remained unchanged<ref>{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112439800|JACAR：A15112439800}}（第5画像目から第6画像目まで）</ref>. Since the criteria for officer Rank and pay were not identical, the regulation was intended to allow each to develop according to its own standards – with pay continuing the Meiji 24 system, while officer Rank reverted to the pre‑Meiji 24 reform system<ref name="明治25th year 勅令第96号の閣議提案" />. Accordingly, the internal regulation for Rank progression was amended to use officer Rank as the standard for conferral, shifting the initial decoration for the Chief of Staff from {{ill|Third Rank (Regular)|ja|正三位|12=draft|12=draft}} to {{ill|Third Rank (Junior)|ja|従三位|12=draft|12=draft}} (similar to the case for military inspectors), and likewise shifting the initial decoration for the Supreme Court President from {{ill|Fourth Rank (Regular)|ja|正四位|12=draft|12=draft}} to {{ill|Third Rank (Junior)|ja|従三位|12=draft|12=draft}} (as it was considered an adjunct position, close to military inspectors and judged to be of higher standing than the head of the Board of Audit)<ref>{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15112272000|JACAR：A15112272000}}（第3画像目から第7画像目まで）</ref>. The internal regulation for awarding decorations was also amended to use officer Rank as the standard – with the initial decoration for ministers, the Privy Council President, generals/admirals, and other Shinninkan set at the second‑class decoration, with advancement possible to the first‑class<ref>「叙勲内則ヲ改定セラル附叙勲内則取扱手続ヲ更定ス」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A15112452200、…</ref>.
In 1900 (Meiji 33), the internal regulation for Rank progression was amended so that high‑Ranking officials, after a new appointment or promotion, would receive their initial Rank inscription after one month, whereas Shinninkan would receive their initial Rank inscription immediately without a one‑month waiting period<ref>「文武官叙位進階内則ヲ改定セラル」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A15113342600、…</ref>{{efn|This amendment was necessary to prevent the criticism of excessively generous conferrals of high Rank, and thus the initial Ranks for Shinninkan and those below were corrected<ref>{{Wikiref|JACAR-A15113342600|JACAR：A15113342600}}（第4画像目）</ref>.}}
==== April 1946 (Showa 21): The Official Appointment and Rank Regulation ==== Following Japan’s acceptance of the {{ill|Potsdam Declaration|ja|ポツダム宣言|12=draft|12=draft}} in 1945 (Showa 20), on April 1, 1946 (Showa 21) the Official Appointment and Rank Regulation (Imperial Ordinance No. 190 of Showa 21) was promulgated and enforced under the Allied occupation<ref name="昭和21st year 勅令第190号官吏任用叙級令">「御署名原本・昭和二十一年・勅令第一九〇号・官吏任用叙級令」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A04017814300、御署名原本・昭和二十一年・勅令第一九〇号・官吏任用叙級令（国立公文書館）（第2画像目）</ref>. In this regulation, other officials (excluding those appointed by personal appointment) were divided into first-, second-, and third‑class officials, and at the same time the High‑Ranking Official Pay Regulation was abolished – with the terms changed so that “imperially appointed officials” became “first‑class officials”, “ceremonial officials” became “second‑class officials”, and “high‑Ranking officials” became “first‑ or second‑class officials”<ref name="昭和21st year 4月1日勅令第193号・高等官官等俸給令廃止">{{Wikiref|JACAR-A04017814600|JACAR：A04017814600}}（第2画像目から第3画像目まで）</ref>; however, officials appointed by personal appointment (Shinninkan) were retained<ref name="昭和21st year 勅令第190号官吏任用叙級令" /> <ref>「御署名原本・昭和二十一年・勅令第一九一号・親任官及諸官級別令」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A04017814400、御署名原本・昭和二十一年・勅令第一九一号・親任官及諸官級別令（国立公文書館）</ref>.
On May 2, 1947 (Showa 22), amendments were made to the Official Appointment and Rank Regulation to revise the provisions concerning officials appointed by personal appointment (excluding special officials), dividing the remaining officials into first-, second‑, and third‑class categories<ref>{{Cite journal|和書|editor=大蔵省印刷局|date=1947-05-02|year=1947|title=官吏任用叙級令の一部を改正する等に関する勅令（昭和22nd year 5月2日勅令第205号）|journal=官報|volume=1947th year 05月02日|issue=物価号外|page=1|publisher=日本マイクロ写真|location=東京|language=ja|accessdate=2024-11-05}}</ref>, and on the following day, with the enforcement of the {{ill|Constitution of Japan|ja|日本国憲法|12=draft|12=draft}}, further amendments were made to conform the regulation to Article 15 of the Constitution by abolishing the provisions for officials appointed by personal appointment (Shinninkan)<ref name="親任官廃止"/><ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.jacar.go.jp/glossary/tochikiko-henten/qa/qa31.html|title=When did the civil service and diplomatic service examinations begin?|accessdate=2024-11-06|author=国立公文書館 アジア歴史資料センター|authorlink=アジア歴史資料センター|website=アジア歴史資料センター|publisher=国立公文書館}}</ref>. Furthermore, whereas previously the Prime Minister, various ministers, and other Shinninkan were appointed by personal appointment, under the new procedures the Prime Minister and the {{ill|Chief Justice of the Supreme Court|ja|最高裁判所長官|12=draft|12=draft}} are appointed by the Emperor pursuant to Article 6 of the {{ill|Constitution of Japan|ja|日本国憲法|12=draft|12=draft}} and related laws<ref>{{Cite journal|和書|editor=大蔵省印刷局|date=1947-04-16|year=1947|title=裁判所法（昭和22nd year 4月16日法律第59号）|journal=官報|volume=昭和|issue=6047|page=118|publisher=日本マイクロ写真|location=東京|language=ja|accessdate=2024-11-10}}</ref>, and other officials’ appointments are certified by the Emperor as part of state acts under Article 7 of the Constitution. The procedure for the Prime Minister’s nomination involves submission by the Speaker of the House of Representatives through the cabinet<ref>{{Cite journal|和書|editor=大蔵省印刷局|date=1947-04-30|year=1947|title=国会法（昭和22nd year 4月30日法律第79号）|journal=官報|volume=昭和|issue=6085|page=283|publisher=日本マイクロ写真|location=東京|language=ja|accessdate=2024-11-10}}</ref>, and the certification of appointment for officials is made by the Prime Minister<ref>{{Cite journal|和書|editor=大蔵省印刷局|date=1947-05-03|year=1947|title=官吏の任免、叙級、休職、復職その他の官吏の身分上の事項に関する手続に関する政令（昭和22nd year 5月3日政令第11号）|journal=官報|volume=1947th year 05月03日|issue=物価号外|page=5|publisher=日本マイクロ写真|location=東京|language=ja|accessdate=2024-11-04}}</ref>.
===Civil Officials=== Civil officials include the {{ill|Prime Minister|ja|Prime Minister of Japan|1=Prime Minister of Japan|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Director of the Japan–Manchuria Affairs Office|ja|対満事務局総裁|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|President of the Privy Council|ja|枢密院議長|12=draft|12=draft}}, the Vice‑President and the Counselor of the Privy Council, the {{ill|Inner Minister|ja|内大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Imperial Household Minister|ja|宮内大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Minister of State|ja|国務大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|文官としての立場での陸軍大臣および海軍大臣も含む。}}</ref>, the {{ill|Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary|ja|特命全権大使|12=draft|12=draft}}, Shinninkan {{ill|judges|ja|判事|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|大審院長及び検事総長は親補職に｜判事は陸海軍将校と同様に終身官であり、検事は裁判所構成法に基づき解任されにくい。}}</ref>, Shinninkan {{ill|prosecutors|ja|検事|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|大審院長及び検事総長は親補職に}}</ref>, the {{ill|Head of the Board of Audit|ja|会計検査院長|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|明治22nd year に会計検査院法制定当初は勅任官であったが、その後親任官へ昇格。}}</ref>, the {{ill|Chief of the Administrative Court|ja|行政裁判所長官|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|明治23rd year に行政裁判法制定当初は勅任官であったが、後に親任官へ。}}</ref>, the {{ill|Governor-General of Korea|ja|朝鮮総督|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|官制では陸海軍大将が任用されるが、後に文官任用も可能となった。}}</ref>, the {{ill|Chief Administrative Officer of the Korean Governor-General's Office|ja|朝鮮総督府政務総監|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Governor of Taiwan|ja|台湾総督|12=draft|12=draft}}<ref>{{efn|官制では陸海軍大将または中将が任用される予定であったが、後に文官任用も可能となり実際には文官が任用された。}}</ref>, the {{ill|Shrine Festival Master|ja|神宮祭主|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|President of the Planning Institute|ja|企画院総裁|12=draft|12=draft}}, the {{ill|Governor of Tokyo|ja|東京都長官|12=draft|12=draft}}, and the {{ill|Regional Governor-General|ja|地方総監|12=draft|12=draft}} among others.
===Military Officials=== Military officials include the {{ill|General of the Army|ja|陸軍大将|12=draft|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Admiral of the Fleet|ja|海軍大将|12=draft|12=draft}}.
==Assistant Positions (Shinpōshoku)== Military officials were distinguished from civil officials by a separate system of appointment and duty orders. In particular, officers were regarded as lifetime officials – even after retirement they retained their Rank. (For example, military officers were classified into active, standby, suspended, or dismissed statuses, and in the case of army officers these classifications were set by earlier regulations; see also the explanatory notes in the “Regulations on Military Officer Appointments”<ref>「陸軍将校免黜条例」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A24011241400、…</ref>.) Consequently, after December 2, 1890 (Meiji 23), the only military officials designated as Shinninkan were the General of the Army and the Admiral of the Fleet<ref>{{efn|明治19th year に初めて親任官を定めた際、陸軍大将、海軍大将に加え、参謀本部長および近衛都督も含まれていたが、その後は大将のみとなった。}}</ref>. Judicial officials were also treated separately – their titles (judge or prosecutor) were kept distinct from their duties, with the Head of the Supreme Court and the Chief Prosecutor regarded as adjunct positions<ref>{{efn|大審院長及び検事総長は親補職に}}</ref>. On November 29, 1890 (Meiji 23), under the Constitution which came into force that year, on December 2 the Regulations for the General Staff (Imperial Ordinance No. 25 of Meiji 22)<ref>「御署名原本・明治二十二年・勅令第二十五号・参謀本部条例制定参軍官制、陸軍参謀本部条例、海軍参謀本部条例廃止」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020035900、…</ref> and the Regulations for the Army Inspection Department (Imperial Ordinance No. 18 of Meiji 20)<ref>「御署名原本・明治二十年・勅令第十八号・監軍部条例」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020011600、…</ref> were amended so that one general or lieutenant general was appointed as the Chief of Staff for the entire Imperial Army and supplemented as an assistant, while one inspector was appointed in the Army Inspection Department and similarly supplemented using a general or lieutenant general<ref name="明治23rd year 勅令第279号参謀本部条例第二条中改正" /> <ref name="明治23rd year 勅令第280号監軍部条例第二条改正" />{{efn|In the Navy, on May 19, 1893 (Meiji 26), a similar amendment was made in the Naval Command Regulations (Imperial Ordinance No. 37 of Meiji 26) to have a general or lieutenant general supplement the Commander of the Naval Command.}}</ref>. In this way, by the Emperor’s {{ill|personal adjunction ceremony|ja|親補式|12=draft|12=draft}}, the position of “Assistant Position (Shinpōshoku)” was established.
On May 1, 1896 (Meiji 29), the document “Matters concerning the Treatment of Those in Assistant Positions and the Head of the Board of Audit” (Imperial Ordinance No. 160 of Meiji 29) stipulated that those holding assistant positions and the Head of the Board of Audit were to receive Shinninkan treatment<ref name="明治29th year 勅令第160号親補ノ職ニ在ル者及会計検査院長待遇ノ件">「親補ノ職ニ在ル者及会計検査院長待遇ノ件」</ref>. The assistant positions were defined within the military hierarchy and, while holding those positions, the officials received Shinninkan treatment<ref name=":0" />. Although no specific Rank was prescribed, the military regulations stated that “assistant positions are to be supplemented by a general or lieutenant general,” so it was not possible for officers below major general to be treated as Shinninkan<ref>{{efn|…}}</ref>. (For instance, in peacetime the divisional commander was not considered “supplemented” by a general but by a lieutenant general, being the largest formation directly controlled by the Emperor<ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治２１年 |pages=77−80|chapter=師団司令部条例（明治21st year 5月14日勅令第27号）|id={{NDLDC|787973/100|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref>{{efn|Examples include cases where a divisional commander in office as a lieutenant general was later conferred Shinninkan status upon promotion to general (e.g. [[長谷川好道]]), or when a divisional commander died in battle and was posthumously promoted to general (e.g. [[栗林忠道]]).}}</ref>. Also, because the Army Minister and the Navy Minister held both military and civil roles, even if they were lieutenant generals, they could issue administrative orders to generals<ref>奥宮正武『大艦巨砲主義の盛衰』〈新戦史シリーズ47〉、朝日ソノラマ、1992nd year 、318頁。</ref>.

==Treatment as Shinninkan==
===Positions Receiving Shinninkan Treatment=== On May 1, 1896 (Meiji 29), the document “Matters concerning the Treatment of Those in Assistant Positions and the Head of the Board of Audit” (Imperial Ordinance No. 160 of Meiji 29) provided that those holding assistant positions and the Head of the Board of Audit were to receive the treatment of Shinninkan<ref name="明治29th year 勅令第160号親補ノ職ニ在ル者及会計検査院長待遇ノ件">「親補ノ職ニ在ル者及会計検査院長待遇ノ件」</ref>{{efn|会計検査院長 was elevated from an imperially appointed official to Shinninkan status.}}. On July 18, 1898 (Meiji 31), the Chief of the Administrative Court was accorded Shinninkan treatment<ref name="明治31st year 勅令第162号行政裁判所長官待遇ノ件">「御署名原本・明治三十一年・勅令第百六十二号・行政裁判所長官待遇ノ件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020346100、…</ref>{{efn|Although his salary was initially unchanged from that of the Privy Council Counselor or Chief Prosecutor, it was raised the following year to match that of the Privy Council President or the Head of the Board of Audit.}}. In the following year his salary was raised to that of the Privy Council President, the Chief Justice, or the Head of the Board of Audit<ref name="枢密院議長副議長顧問官並書記官長書記官議長秘書官年俸（明治24th year 7月27日勅令第96号） 〔明治21st year 勅令第23号の全部改正〕" /> <ref name="判事検事官等俸給令（明治27th year 2月15日勅令第17号）" /> <ref>{{Cite book|和書|editor=内閣官報局|date=1912-10|title=法令全書|publisher=内閣官報局|location=東京|volume=明治３２年 |page=179|chapter=明治二十四年勅令第九十八号（行政裁判所長官評定官年俸ノ件）中改正ノ件（明治32nd year 4月10日勅令第136号）|id={{NDLDC|788011/471|format=NDLJP}} }}</ref>.
On August 29, 1910 (Meiji 43), when the {{ill|Governor-General of Korea|ja|朝鮮総督府|12=draft|12=draft}} was established, officials from the former Korean government’s agencies who were considered part of the new Governor-General’s Office and who had previously been treated as Shinninkan under Korean law were granted Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・明治四十三年・勅令第三百十九号・朝鮮総督府設置ニ関スル件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020863200、…</ref>. In September of the same year, a Central Council ({{ill|Korean Governor-General’s Central Council|ja|朝鮮総督府中枢院|12=draft|12=draft}}) was established and its Vice-President was accorded Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・明治四十三年・勅令第三百五十五号・朝鮮総督府中枢院官制」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020866800、…</ref>.
On July 28, 1911 (Meiji 44), the President of the {{ill|Japan Exhibition|ja|博覧会|12=draft|12=draft}} was granted Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・明治四十四年・勅令第二百十二号・日本大博覧会会長ノ待遇ニ関スル件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03020909500、…</ref>.
On April 14, 1916 (Taisho 5), among temporary staff sent to attend the Allied Economic Conference, the Special Commissioner for the conference was accorded Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・大正五年・勅令第百八号・連合国経済会議ニ参列セシムルタメ臨時職員設置」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021070500、…</ref>.
On March 26, 1921 (Taisho 10), the advisor to the Korean Governor-General’s Central Council was granted Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・大正十年・勅令第百六十八号・朝鮮総督府中枢院官制中改正」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021323100、…</ref>.
On June 14, 1927 (Showa 2), an Administrative System Deliberation Council was established; for its members, if serving in an official capacity they received treatment according to their office, otherwise they were given Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・昭和二年・勅令第一六八号・行政制度審議会官制」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021654000、…</ref>. On December 7 of the same year, the President of the {{ill|Tokyo Appellate Court|ja|東京控訴院長|12=draft|12=draft}} was granted Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・昭和二年・勅令第三四八号・東京控訴院長ノ待遇ニ関スル件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021672000、…</ref>.
On June 20, 1931 (Showa 6), an ad hoc Administrative and Financial Deliberation Council was established, and among its members those with academic or professional expertise were granted Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・昭和六年・勅令第一四〇号・臨時行政財政審議会官制（第二百五十七号ヲ以テ本号中改正第二百九十二号ヲ以テ廃止）」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03021811900、…</ref>.
On September 9, 1938 (Showa 13), an ad hoc diplomatic advisor position was created within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and was accorded Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・昭和十三年・勅令第六三二号・臨時外務省ニ外交顧問ヲ置クノ件」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03022231000、…</ref>.
On October 27, 1944 (Showa 19), an ad hoc Cabinet Advisor position was established and granted Shinninkan treatment<ref>「御署名原本・昭和十九年・勅令第六〇四号・内閣顧問臨時設置制」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03022315100、…</ref>.
===Particularly, Those Granted Special Shinninkan Treatment=== For certain positions, officials who had served a prescribed number of years or rendered especially distinguished service – even if their office was not inherently a Shinninkan position – could be granted Shinninkan treatment based on the “Internal Regulation for Granting Shinninkan Treatment.” According to this regulation, the following officials were eligible:
;Internal Regulation for Granting Shinninkan Treatment (Decided April 28, Showa 17) :The regulation is defined as follows: :For imperially appointed civil officials who satisfy one of the following and have rendered especially outstanding service, a petition for granting Shinninkan treatment may be submitted: # Presidents of Imperial Universities and of the Keijo and Taipei Imperial Universities who have served as first‑class officials for 8 or more years. # Heads of the Hokkaido Prefecture, police commissioners, or prefectural governors who have served as first‑class officials for 6 or more years. # Deputy ministers of each ministry who have served as first‑class officials for 6 or more years. # Other imperially appointed civil officials who have served as first‑class officials for 15 or more years. # In cases under either clause 1 or 2, the number of officials granted Shinninkan treatment is limited to three per category. :Additionally, Cabinet Secretaries or Directors of the Legal Bureau with particularly outstanding records may be petitioned for special Shinninkan treatment. :Similarly, for Army or Navy administrative officers with important roles in occupied areas and outstanding service records, a petition may be submitted. :Moreover, those who have previously held Shinninkan status or received such treatment may also be considered.
;Examples of specific decrees granting “special Shinninkan treatment”: * [[片岡七郎]] (Head of the Naval Administration Headquarters, Navy Lieutenant General), November 20, 1906 (Meiji 39)<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 海軍艦政本部長海軍中将 片岡七郎」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023374600、…</ref>. * [[後藤新平]] (Vice-President of the Settlement Bureau), June 20, 1910 (Meiji 43)<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 拓殖局副総裁 男爵後藤新平」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023380500、…</ref>. * [[一木喜徳郎]] (Director of the Legal Bureau), December 21, 1912 (Taisho 1)<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 法制局長官法学博士 一木喜徳郎」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023388200、…</ref>. * [[清野長太郎]] (Head of the Reconstruction Bureau), September 16, 1925 (Taisho 14)<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 復興局長官 清野長太郎」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023441100、…</ref>. * [[真崎甚三郎]] (Vice Chief of Staff, Army Lieutenant General), January 7, 1932 (Showa 7)<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 参謀次長陸軍中将 真崎甚三郎」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023464200、…</ref>. * [[井上成美]] (Deputy Navy Minister, Navy Lieutenant General), August 4, 1944 (Showa 19)<ref>「特ニ親任官ノ待遇ヲ賜フ 海軍次官 井上成美」JACAR（アジア歴史資料センター）Ref.A03023548800、…</ref>.
==Abuse of the Military Councilor System in the Imperial Army== In the Imperial Army, there were cases in which a lieutenant general holding an assistant (Shinpōshoku) position would concurrently hold a non‑assistant post without a formal demotion – effectively using the position of Military Councilor as his principal office. Lieutenant General [[額田坦]], the last Chief of the Army Personnel Bureau, commented, “This should be regarded as an abuse of the Military Councilor system.”<ref name=":9">[[額田坦]]『陸軍省人事局長の回想』（芙蓉書房、1977〈昭和52nd year 〉）、227頁。</ref>
For example:
; [[鈴木孝雄]] : An army officer (2nd term graduate of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Academy|ja|陸軍士官学校|12=draft|12=draft}}). In February 1924 (Taisho 13) he was supplemented as the commander of the {{ill|14th Division|ja|第14師団|12=draft|12=draft}}. In August of the same year he was transferred to serve as the head of the {{ill|Army Technical Headquarters|ja|陸軍技術本部|12=draft|12=draft}} (a non‑assistant position). In July 1926 (Taisho 15) he was supplemented as a Military Councilor while continuing as head of the Army Technical Headquarters. In July 1927 (Showa 2) he was appointed as a general, and on March 8, 1928 (Showa 3) he ceased concurrently serving as head of the Army Technical Headquarters and became exclusively a Military Councilor. (He served as a Military Councilor in his principal role from July 1926 to March 1933 – a total of 6 years and 8 months.)
; [[土肥原賢二]] : An army officer (16th term graduate of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Academy|ja|陸軍士官学校|12=draft|12=draft}}). In March 1937 (Showa 12) he was supplemented as the commander of the {{ill|14th Division|ja|第14師団|12=draft|12=draft}}. In June 1938 (Showa 13) he was assigned to the General Staff. In May 1939 (Showa 14) he was supplemented as the commander of the {{ill|5th Army|ja|第5軍|12=draft|12=draft}}, and in June 1940 (Showa 15) returned to the General Staff; later in September of that year he was supplemented as a Military Councilor and in October he concurrently assumed the post of {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Academy|ja|陸軍士官学校|12=draft|12=draft}} Head (a non‑assistant position). In April 1941 (Showa 16) he was appointed as a general; in June he was supplemented as the Army Air Service Chief. (He served as Military Councilor in his principal role from September 1940 to June 1941 – a total of 9 months.)
; [[篠塚義男]] : An army officer (17th term graduate of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Academy|ja|陸軍士官学校|12=draft|12=draft}}). In June 1938 (Showa 13) he was supplemented as the commander of the {{ill|10th Division|ja|第10師団|12=draft|12=draft}}. In September 1939 (Showa 14) he was supplemented as the commander of the {{ill|1st Army|ja|第1軍|12=draft|12=draft}}. In July 1941 (Showa 16) he was supplemented as a Military Councilor while concurrently serving as the Head of the Imperial Japanese Army Academy (a non‑assistant position). In July 1942 (Showa 17) he entered the reserves on request<ref>『陸軍省人事局長の回想』 411頁。</ref> (He served as Military Councilor in his principal role from July 1941 to July 1942 – a total of 1 year).
==Former Official Honors== Among the Shinninkan, those who held offices such as the {{ill|Prime Minister|ja|Prime Minister of Japan|1=Prime Minister of Japan|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Minister of State|ja|国務大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|President of the Privy Council|ja|枢密院議長|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Imperial Household Minister|ja|宮内大臣|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Inner Minister|ja|内大臣|12=draft|12=draft}} would, if they had served for a sufficient number of years, upon retirement be granted former official honors by special imperial decree. Such honors—conferring, for example, preferential seating at the {{ill|Imperial Court Order|ja|宮中席次|12=draft|12=draft}}—were awarded as follows:
; Former Official Honor Award Regulation for the Prime Minister (Approved September 6, Showa 14) : The regulation is set out as follows: # For former Prime Ministers who served for at least 4 years. # For those who served as Prime Minister more than twice. # And for those who had previously received former official honors as either the Privy Council President, Minister of State, Imperial Household Minister, or Inner Minister. ; (Similar provisions apply for former Ministers of State and for former Privy Council Presidents, with detailed clauses on how service years are totaled.)
